title: Two loads
topic: A friend is timing two loads of laundry before heading out
blurb: A friend is trying to wash and dry two loads before leaving the house.
prompt: A friend just texted this in the group chat. If one line doesn't add up, tap it.

segments.label: The deadline
segments.text: I have to leave in two hours, and I've still got two loads that need to be washed and dried.

segments.label: The machines
segments.text: The washer takes 30 minutes a load, and the dryer next to it takes 45.

segments.label: The sigh
segments.text: That's 75 minutes start to finish for one load, so two loads is two and a half hours. I'm not going to make it.

segments.label: The fallback
segments.text: If anyone's nearby later, I may need to borrow a shirt.

conclusion: 75 minutes a load times two is two and a half hours, so I won't be done before I leave.

flaws.original: I can wash the second load while the first one dries: 30 plus 45 plus 45 is two hours. I can just make it.
flaws.corrupted: That's 75 minutes start to finish for one load, so two loads is two and a half hours. I'm not going to make it.

diagnosis_choices.label: Wash load two while load one dries: 30 + 45 + 45 is 2 hours flat.
The dryer is the slow step, so two loads only take 45 + 45 = 90 minutes, leaving 30 minutes to spare.
Run both loads in the washer together so the whole wash-and-dry cycle finishes in 75 minutes.
Two hours is 120 minutes and 75 + 75 is 150, so skipping 15 minutes of drying per load gets you out on time.

fix_choices.label: Start load two in the washer as soon as load one hits the dryer: 30 + 45 + 45 = 120 min.
Count only the two 45-minute dry cycles (90 minutes total) since the washer runs inside them.
Combine both loads into one large wash-and-dry cycle so everything finishes in 75 minutes.
Cut each dry cycle from 45 minutes down to 30 minutes so both loads finish in two hours.

flaws.explanation: The washer doesn't have to sit and watch the dryer. Wash the second load while the first one dries — two hours on the dot.
flaws.why_tempting: 75 plus 75 is clean arithmetic. It's easy to line the two loads up end to end and forget the machines can work at the same time.
flaws.catch_rule: When two machines can run at once, start the next wash while the first load dries — don't add the full cycles together.
flaws.hint: When the first load moves into the dryer, what's the washer doing?

practice.problem: A printer takes 4 minutes a document, and the binder next to it takes 6. A friend says two documents will take 20 minutes because 10 × 2 = 20. What's wrong?
practice.answer: The second document can print while the first one is being bound: 4 + 6 + 6 = 16 minutes, not 20.

clean_segments: I have to leave in two hours, and I've still got two loads that need to be washed and dried.
The washer takes 30 minutes a load, and the dryer next to it takes 45.
I can wash the second load while the first one dries: 30 plus 45 plus 45 is two hours. I can just make it.
If anyone's nearby later, I may need to borrow a shirt.
clean_conclusion: Wash the second load while the first one dries. That's two hours, just in time.

diagnosis: Two hours is 120 minutes, which leaves zero buffer for folding and moving wet clothes between machines.
If you only need one shirt before leaving, you don't need both loads washed and dried in two hours.
Saying 'two hours' ignores the 10 minutes it takes to get dressed and walk out the door.
Two full loads of laundry can always be combined into one heavy-duty cycle when you're in a rush.
fix: Wash only the load with the shirt you need and leave load two for tonight.
Budget 10 minutes for switching machines so your real window is 110 minutes.
Combine both loads into one cycle to finish well inside two hours.
Push your departure back 30 minutes so both loads finish comfortably.

diagnosis: Because the washer is 15 minutes faster than the dryer, load two sits wet for 15 minutes and adds 15 minutes to the schedule.
30 minutes plus 45 minutes is 65 minutes per load, not 75 minutes.
Dryers take longer on a second load because the lint trap fills up, so 45 minutes understates load two.
Running a washer and dryer side by side on the same circuit trips the breaker, so they can't run together.
fix: Add 15 minutes of wait time while load two sits in the washer waiting for the dryer.
Re-add 30 + 45 as 65 minutes per load (130 minutes for two).
Clean the lint trap between loads so the second dry stays at 45 minutes.
Run the dryer on low heat while the washer runs so they don't trip the breaker.

diagnosis: You don't need to borrow a shirt — load one finishes in 75 minutes, 45 minutes before you have to leave.
Borrowing a shirt won't help because load two still needs another 90 minutes in the dryer.
Even if both loads take 150 minutes, you'll be back in time to fold load two later.
Asking to borrow a shirt assumes the shirt you want is in the second load instead of the first.
fix: Put the shirt you plan to wear in load one so it's dry in 75 minutes.
Start both machines in sequence and you won't need to borrow anything.
Ask to borrow a shirt only if the second dry cycle runs past 45 minutes.
Hang the second load to dry while you're out and wear something from load one.
